transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... my wife is the one who wanted me to come in. She thinks I'm not eating enough. 

I don't really see the problem, though. Most days I just have my coffee and a piece of toast in the morning, and... maybe some soup or a few vegetables later on. Big meals just feel unnecessary at my age. That's really it.
Do you avoid eating more because you're worried about gaining weight or because of how you perceive your body shape or size?

Well... I don't know if I'd use the word worried. 

But... when my wife tries to put butter on things, or... when she serves me a big, full plate, I just... I get a little nervous, I guess. I don't want to start putting weight back on. I've worked hard to keep things under control, and... I just don't want to lose that control. That's all it is.
Have you ever gone out of your way to avoid gaining weight, like skipping meals, exercising a lot more, or limiting certain foods even if you weren't hungry?

Well... I don't really do all that. I'm 78, so I'm certainly not out there exercising a lot. Just... taking my walks. 

And I don't think of it as skipping meals. I just... eat what I feel like I need. I keep away from the heavy things, sure, but... I wouldn't say I go out of my way. It's just my routine.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or do you consider your weight to be much lower than normal for your age and health?

Well... my regular doctor did mention something about the scale... said the number was getting a bit low. 

But I don't see it that way. Being a bit lighter just... it makes it easier to get around. I can still tend to the garden, and it's easier on the joints when I take my walks. So... I think it's fine.
When you talk about keeping things under control and not wanting to gain weight, do you feel like your weight or body shape has a strong influence on how you see yourself or your self-worth?

Well... I don't know about self-worth. That sounds a bit dramatic. 

But... I suppose I do pay attention to how things fit. Like, if my belt feels a notch looser... I feel like I've done right by myself. Kept my discipline. 

But... if I happen to catch sight of myself in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit rounded... I don't like it. I feel... sloppy, I guess. Disappointed in myself. It just means I've let things slip.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see your body differently than others might see it, or do you feel like you notice things that others wouldn't?

I don't know about how others see it. I don't really ask them. 

I just... I see what's there. I see if things are getting loose, or if they're... not. I don't think I'm seeing anything that isn't real. It's just my body. I know what it's supposed to look like.
When you look at yourself and notice that you’re a bit rounder, do you think others would see it the same way, or do you think you notice it more than they would?

I don't really know what other people see. I don't ask. 

I just... I notice it. It's my body, so I'm the one who sees it. I don't pay much mind to what anyone else thinks about it.
Do you find that your thoughts about your weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself overall, like whether you feel good or bad about who you are?

I thought we just went over this. 

It's... like I said a minute ago. If my belt is a notch looser, I feel fine. Like I've done right by myself. And if I look in the mirror and see my stomach looking round... well, I feel disappointed. Sloppy. 

That's really about as deep as it goes. I don't sit around analyzing who I am as a person.
Would you say the weight you’ve lost was something you intentionally wanted, or has it happened without you actively trying?

I don't know if I'd use those words. I just... eat what I think I should. 

If the weight comes off, it comes off. I haven't really sat down and made a big plan out of it. I'm just going about my days.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you ever feel like you see yourself as heavier than you actually are?

I don't... I just see what's there. 

I'm not imagining things, if that's what you mean. I look, and I see my reflection. I don't think it's any heavier or lighter than the reality of it. It's just my body.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, does the thought of gaining even a little weight feel unacceptable to you, or does it feel like something you absolutely need to avoid?

Well... I suppose it's something I try to avoid. 

Like... when my wife cooks. If she tries to put butter on things, or if she hands me a plate that's just too full... I get a bit anxious about it. I don't want to start putting the weight back on. I've worked to keep things under control, and... I just don't want to lose that.
When you turn down the food your wife offers, is it mostly because you're afraid of gaining weight, or is it more about just sticking to what feels right to you?

I don't know if I'd say I'm afraid. I just... I guess I prefer to stick to what I know. 

It's just how I do things now. I'm used to it, and... it just feels better to keep it that way. I haven't really thought about it much deeper than that.
Do you ever go out of your way to avoid eating with other people, or do you have specific rules or rituals around eating that help you stick to your routine?

I don't really... avoid people. My wife and I mostly just eat at home anyway. We don't have a lot of company these days, so it doesn't really come up. 

And... no, I don't have rules. I just eat my meals. There's no rituals or anything like that. I just do what I normally do.
Do you feel that changing your eating habits, even slightly, would lead to a loss of control over your weight or how you feel about yourself?

Well... I suppose. Like I was saying before, with the butter or... or if she gives me too much on a plate. If I start changing things, I just get a bit nervous that the weight will come back. 

I've got it under control right now, and... I just don't want to lose that.
Would you say your eating habits are mostly about keeping your weight where it feels right, or more about just doing what feels natural to you at this point in your life?
I suppose... maybe a bit of both. It's just what I do now. It keeps things where they should be, and... well, it feels natural enough to me at this point. I just don't see a need to mess with it.
Would you say that your concern about your weight or the way you look is more about how you actually are, or is it more about how you feel you should be?

I don't know about... how I should be. It's more about how I feel day to day. 

Like... if I put my pants on and the belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It's a good feeling. But... if I happen to catch sight of my stomach in the mirror and it looks even the least bit rounded... I just feel sloppy. Disappointed in myself, I guess. So I just try to keep it where it needs to be.
